meta.storyTitle: Pointer and Locator as the shared building blocks for naming content

override.reason: Automated design review is retired/unavailable while being rewritten. Revision 3 adds the real PointerPathValidator implementation (sc6) this Story now owns, plus syncing sc6's hldContextSlice copy verbatim with the HLD. User approved explicitly in chat for this batch of 6 artifacts.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Alternative a2 wins: one canonical TypeScript type per Story (Pointer/Locator, Scope, ReviewTargets, CommentEntry+round), with per-review-type validator functions running against the canonical type and a thin per-consumer transformer reshaping it for whichever LLM structured-output schema that consumer actually parses reliably, mirroring the existing CliProvider input/output transformer pattern.

ownedContracts.name: Locator + Pointer
ownedContracts.purpose: The uniform way every Scope and ReviewTargets entry names a piece of content: a Pointer to an existing authored file plus an optional Locator pinning an exact region within it, per k2.

ownedContracts.name: Pointer staleness check
ownedContracts.purpose: One staleness-detection function signature shared by every Pointer consumer (Scope and ReviewTargets alike), per k5 -- no consumer defines its own.

ownedContracts.name: Pointer path validation
ownedContracts.purpose: One repo-root-escape check shared by every Pointer consumer (Scope and ReviewTargets alike), per the Epic's own nonFunctional security note -- no consumer defines its own, mirroring sc2's staleness-check pattern. Closes a cross-Story gap found in a controller-led cross-LLD review on 2026-11-19: s1's error-paths deferred this check to 's2's ScopeValidator' informally, but neither s2 nor s3 ever picked it up.

boundary.internal: The specific set of currently-known LocatorKind string literals (symbol/lineRange/docSection) is s1's own enumeration; because every consumer treats `Locator.kind` as an opaque string rather than exhaustively switching on a closed union, s1 can add a new literal later without forcing s2/s3/s4 to change, satisfying ac2/lc1.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Which named artifact-kind fields Scope carries beyond def/hld/lld/plan/tasks (e.g. a future named kind) and the exact per-review-type ScopeValidator implementations are s2's own; no other Story's type depends on Scope, since nothing in the Epic's Story graph consumes s2.
ReviewTargets' own reset-on-new-round mechanics (how the entries list is rebuilt rather than merged) stay internal to s3; no other Story's type depends on ReviewTargets.

CommentEntry does not reference Pointer/Locator at all, so s4 needs neither sc1 nor sc2. The round-stamping mechanics (how a new attempt's round number is assigned) and the same-artifact-only scoping of Comments across a chain stay internal to s4; the full ReviewContext container embedding Scope and ReviewTargets alongside round/comments is explicitly deferred (Epic Non-Goals), since no Story in this graph depends on all of s2, s3 and s4 together.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase A — foundational Pointer/Locator + staleness contract

nonFunctional.performance: The staleness check (sc2) is a single hash comparison against already-read file content; it adds no I/O beyond the read the controller already performs to populate a Pointer's contentHash.
nonFunctional.security: Pointer.path is repo-relative and must resolve within the registered repo root; validators (k3) reject a Pointer whose path escapes that root, consistent with the repo-registry strict-contract rule elsewhere in this codebase.

summary.prose: This Story defines Locator and Pointer, the two foundational types every other piece of ReviewContext uses to name a piece of content: a Pointer references an existing authored file (optionally with a content hash recorded at build time), and an optional Locator pins an exact region within it. It also defines one shared, pure staleness-detection function so every consumer (Scope, ReviewTargets) checks a Pointer's freshness the same way, with no I/O inside the check itself.

api.name: PointerStalenessCheck
api.signature: type PointerStalenessCheck = (pointer: Pointer, currentContentHash: string) => StalenessResult

parameters.name: pointer
parameters.purpose: The Pointer whose recorded contentHash is being checked for staleness.

parameters.name: currentContentHash
parameters.purpose: The sha256 hex digest of pointer.path's current content, computed by the caller (createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')) before calling this function -- the function performs no I/O itself.

returns.meaning: {stale, checkedAt}: whether pointer.contentHash (when present) differs from currentContentHash, and the ISO-8601 timestamp the comparison was made.

preconditions: pointer.contentHash may be absent (a Pointer built without recording a hash); in that case the function returns stale:false -- there is nothing to compare against, so absence is not staleness.
postconditions: The function is pure: given the same two arguments it always returns the same stale value; only checkedAt varies by wall-clock time.

api.name: PointerPathValidator
api.signature: type PointerPathValidator = (pointer: Pointer, registeredRepoRoot: string) => PathValidationResult

parameters.name: pointer
parameters.purpose: The Pointer whose path is being checked for escaping the registered repo root.

parameters.name: registeredRepoRoot
parameters.purpose: The absolute path of the registered repo root the caller is validating against, obtained the same way the repo-registry strict-contract rule elsewhere in this codebase does (the registered repo's own root).

returns.meaning: {ok, violations}: whether pointer.path, once resolved via path.resolve(registeredRepoRoot, pointer.path), stays within registeredRepoRoot; a violation names the escaping path when it does not.

postconditions: The function is pure: it only normalizes and compares two strings (via path.resolve, the same normalization src/db/repos.ts's own repo-path comparison already uses) and returns a result; it performs no file-system I/O and mutates nothing.

dataModelChanges.details: interface Locator { readonly kind: LocatorKind | string; readonly value: string } where type LocatorKind = 'symbol' | 'lineRange' | 'docSection' (known kinds; the set is open, not exhaustive -- every consumer reads kind structurally, e.g. a lookup by string key, never an exhaustive switch with no default, per the HLD's own risky-bits mitigation). value stays one opaque string per kind (a symbol name, 'startLine-endLine', or a doc-section id) -- the caller that builds a Locator already knows the format for its own kind; this Story does not introduce per-kind structured typing (a2 rejected). Lands in src/workflow/artifact-core/types.ts, the existing home for shared plain-interface types in this part of the codebase.

interface Pointer { readonly path: string; readonly section?: Locator; readonly contentHash?: string }. path is a repo-relative path to an existing authored file (DEF.md/HLD.md/LLD.md/source); never a generated extract. contentHash, when present, is the sha256 hex digest of path's content at the time this Pointer was built, computed with createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex') -- the same idiom already used for entity ids and for the lifecycle revision's own contentHash. Pointer MUST stay a plain TypeScript interface (no sealed/closed type, no class) so a future structural subtype -- e.g. the sibling standalone security-extension-points Story's planned SecurityPointer, which the user has decided will be `interface SecurityPointer extends Pointer` -- can add its own fields (trustBoundaryId, taintPathStepIndex) without this Story needing to change; that future subtype is out of this Story's scope and is not modeled here. Lands in src/workflow/artifact-core/types.ts alongside Locator.

interface StalenessResult { readonly stale: boolean; readonly checkedAt: string } (checkedAt is ISO-8601). Returned by PointerStalenessCheck. Lands beside Locator/Pointer in src/workflow/artifact-core/types.ts.

interface PathValidationResult { readonly ok: boolean; readonly violations: readonly string[] }, returned by PointerPathValidator. Lands beside Locator/Pointer/StalenessResult in src/workflow/artifact-core/types.ts.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: This Story is sc1's owner; Locator and Pointer are implemented exactly as sc1's interfaceSketch describes, with Pointer kept plain-interface-extensible per the resolved cross-design open question on the future SecurityPointer subtype.

This Story is sc2's owner; PointerStalenessCheck implements sc2's interfaceSketch exactly -- a pure, synchronous function taking a pre-computed currentContentHash, with no I/O inside it, matching sc2's own nonFunctional performance note.

This Story is sc6's owner; PointerPathValidator implements sc6's interfaceSketch exactly -- a pure, synchronous function using the same path.resolve-based normalization src/db/repos.ts's own repo-path comparison already uses, closing the gap this LLD's s2/s3 siblings left unaddressed.

errorCases.scenario: A caller passes a currentContentHash to PointerStalenessCheck that was computed with a different scheme than this Story's established createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex') idiom (e.g. base64 instead of hex, or hashed over normalized rather than raw bytes).
errorCases.detection: PointerStalenessCheck performs a plain string comparison between pointer.contentHash and currentContentHash; it has no way to detect which hashing scheme produced either string, since both are opaque strings to the function.
errorCases.response: No error is raised. The mismatched encoding simply makes the two strings unequal, so the comparison reports stale:true even though the file may not actually have changed -- a false positive caused entirely by a caller-side hashing-convention violation, not something this pure function can catch.
errorCases.userImpact: A Pointer could be reported stale incorrectly if some future caller does not follow the established sha256-hex idiom; this is a caller-discipline concern, not a defect in PointerStalenessCheck itself.

errorCases.scenario: The file at pointer.path no longer exists (deleted or moved) since the Pointer was built.
errorCases.detection: PointerStalenessCheck itself never reads pointer.path -- it only compares two already-computed strings -- so it cannot detect a missing file. Detection happens one level up, at the caller's own file-read step (an ENOENT or equivalent) when it tries to compute currentContentHash before calling this function at all.
errorCases.response: Out of this Story's scope: file I/O and its error handling belong to the caller (the controller or a consuming Story's validator), not to the pure Locator/Pointer/PointerStalenessCheck contract this Story defines. This Story's contract assumes currentContentHash is already available by the time PointerStalenessCheck is called.
errorCases.userImpact: None directly from this Story's types; a caller that does not handle a missing-file read error before calling PointerStalenessCheck would surface that failure through its own error path, not through a StalenessResult.

errorCases.scenario: A Pointer.path value that would resolve outside the registered repo root (e.g. containing '..' segments) is passed to PointerPathValidator.
errorCases.detection: PointerPathValidator resolves pointer.path against registeredRepoRoot via path.resolve (the same normalization src/db/repos.ts's own repo-path comparison already uses, per 'Compared post-path.resolve so trailing slashes / `..` segments' normalize') and checks the result starts with registeredRepoRoot.
errorCases.response: Returns ok:false with a violation naming the escaping path. This closes the gap found in a cross-LLD review: earlier this Story deferred the check to 's2's ScopeValidator' informally with no shared contract backing it; sc6 now gives s2 and s3 a real function to call on every Pointer-typed field before sending a Scope/ReviewTargets instance for review.
errorCases.userImpact: A Pointer that would escape the registered repo root is rejected with a named violation instead of silently passing through to review.

edgeCases.input: A Pointer with no contentHash at all (never recorded at build time).
edgeCases.expected: PointerStalenessCheck returns stale:false -- there is nothing to compare against, so an absent contentHash is not treated as staleness, per the function's documented precondition.

edgeCases.input: A Pointer.contentHash that is present but an empty string.
edgeCases.expected: An empty string is still a 'present' value (not undefined), so it is compared literally against currentContentHash like any other string; it is almost certainly unequal to a real sha256 hex digest, so this reports stale:true -- not a special case, just the ordinary comparison outcome for an unusual recorded value.

edgeCases.input: A Locator with kind set to a string that is not one of the three currently-known literals (symbol/lineRange/docSection) -- e.g. a future kind introduced by a different Story.
edgeCases.expected: Accepted without error: kind is typed `LocatorKind | string`, so any string is structurally valid. Consumers reading kind must do so via a non-exhaustive lookup (e.g. a string-keyed branch), never an exhaustive switch with no default, per ac2/lc1.

edgeCases.input: A Locator.value string whose format does not match the convention expected for its own kind (e.g. a 'lineRange' kind with a value that is not actually formatted 'startLine-endLine').
edgeCases.expected: This Story's types do not validate value's internal format per kind -- that interpretation and validation responsibility belongs to whichever consumer reads a Locator of that specific kind, not to the Locator type itself.

alternativesConsidered.name: Exactly-as-sketched minimal types: opaque-string Locator, plain Pointer, pure synchronous staleness comparator
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Implement sc1/sc2 literally as the HLD's own interface sketches: Locator{kind:string,value:string}, Pointer{path,section?,contentHash?}, and a pure PointerStalenessCheck(pointer, currentContentHash) => StalenessResult that only compares two hex strings.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Locator.kind stays a plain string (LocatorKind | string) and Locator.value stays one opaque string per kind (symbol name, 'startLine-endLine', or doc-section id) -- the caller that builds a Locator already knows how to format value for its kind; no cross-kind structured typing is introduced. Pointer stays exactly {path, section?: Locator, contentHash?: string}. PointerStalenessCheck is a pure, synchronous function: it takes the Pointer and an already-computed currentContentHash (the caller reads the file and runs createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex'), matching the repo's established content-hashing idiom) and returns {stale, checkedAt} from a plain string comparison -- no I/O inside the function itself, matching sc2's nonFunctional performance note ('adds no I/O beyond the read the controller already performs').
pros: Matches the HLD's own interfaceSketch for sc1/sc2 verbatim -- no deviation for s2/s3 to adapt to later
The smallest shape that fully satisfies ac1/ac2/ac3: file+region naming, open extensibility, uniform staleness reporting
A pure, synchronous staleness function is trivially unit-testable with plain string fixtures, no mocking of file I/O needed
cons: Callers must remember to compute currentContentHash themselves (read file + sha256) before calling the staleness check -- the function does not do it for them

alternativesConsidered.name: Structured per-kind Locator.value (discriminated union keyed by kind)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Replace Locator's single opaque `value: string` with a discriminated union typing value's shape per known kind (e.g. {kind:'lineRange', start:number, end:number} vs {kind:'symbol', name:string}).
alternativesConsidered.approach: Define Locator as a union of concrete shapes, one per known LocatorKind literal, each with its own strongly-typed value fields instead of one opaque string a caller must format/parse by convention.
pros: Stronger compile-time typing for the three currently-known kinds: a lineRange locator's start/end are real numbers, not a parsed 'startLine-endLine' string
cons: Directly contradicts lc1/ac2's open-extensibility requirement: a discriminated union is closed by construction, so a future locator kind would require a new union member and a breaking change for every exhaustive switch -- exactly what ac2 says must not happen

The HLD's sc1 interfaceSketch explicitly chose `kind: LocatorKind | string` and one opaque `value: string` for this reason; this alternative reopens a decision the HLD already made and would need an HLD back-flow, not just an LLD choice
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Directly contradicts lc1/ac2's open-extensibility requirement by closing Locator's value into a per-kind discriminated union, and deviates from sc1's own published interfaceSketch, which already chose the open opaque-string shape for this reason.

alternativesConsidered.name: Self-contained async staleness check that reads and hashes the file itself
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Give PointerStalenessCheck a single-argument async signature that reads pointer.path from disk and computes its own sha256 hash internally, instead of taking a pre-computed currentContentHash.
alternativesConsidered.approach: PointerStalenessCheck(pointer: Pointer) => Promise<StalenessResult> reads the file at pointer.path itself, hashes it, and compares against pointer.contentHash -- the caller passes only the Pointer, not a separately-computed hash.
pros: Simpler call site: one argument instead of two, nothing for the caller to remember to pre-compute
cons: Directly contradicts sc2's published interfaceSketch, which is explicitly synchronous and takes `currentContentHash` as its second parameter -- every consumer (s2, s3) already expects that exact signature

Duplicates file I/O the controller already performs when it populates a Pointer's contentHash in the first place, directly contradicting sc2's own nonFunctional performance note that the staleness check 'adds no I/O beyond the read the controller already performs'
Makes the staleness check async and I/O-bound, which both s2 and s3's LLDs (not yet written) would then have to accommodate, rather than reusing one simple pure function
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Contradicts sc2's exact published synchronous signature and its own nonFunctional performance note by making the staleness check asynchronous and self-reading, duplicating I/O the controller already performs.

erDefinition.narrative: Shows the three types this Story introduces and their one relationship: a Pointer optionally carries a Locator (via its `section` field) that pins an exact region within the file the Pointer names; PointerStalenessCheck (not itself a class) consumes a Pointer and produces a StalenessResult.

Locator.description: Pins an exact region within an authored file: a symbol name, a line range, or a doc-section id, per an open (non-exhaustive) kind discriminant.

kind.description: LocatorKind | string -- a known literal (symbol/lineRange/docSection) or any future string; read structurally, never via exhaustive switch.

value.description: One opaque string formatted per kind: a symbol name, 'startLine-endLine', or a doc-section id.

Pointer.description: References an existing authored file directly (never a generated extract), optionally with an exact region and a content hash recorded at build time. Stays plain-interface-extensible so a future structural subtype (e.g. the sibling security-extension-points Story's planned SecurityPointer) can extend it.

path.description: Repo-relative path to an existing authored file (DEF.md/HLD.md/LLD.md/source).

section.description: An optional Locator pinning the exact region within `path` this Pointer names.

contentHash.description: sha256 hex digest of path's content when this Pointer was built, via createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex').

StalenessResult.description: The outcome of comparing a Pointer's recorded contentHash against the referenced file's current content.

stale.description: True when pointer.contentHash is present and differs from the currentContentHash passed to PointerStalenessCheck.

checkedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when the comparison was made.
